Safety instructions: - Do not open, modify, or tamper with high-voltage components.
- Repairs must be performed by qualified personnel only.
- In case of an accident, do not touch exposed orange cables or components.
- Avoid water or snow contact with high-voltage areas.
- Turn off the vehicle before servicing any electrical systems.
- Risk of severe burns, electric shock, or death if safety instructions are ignored.
Conservation of the high-voltage battery: - Avoid deep discharge and long-term full charging.
- Park the vehicle in the shade or in a garage when possible.
- Keep the battery charge between 20% and 80% for longevity.
- Use scheduled charging to delay battery aging.
- Reduce use of fast charging to prevent thermal stress.
Charging the high-voltage battery: - Use compatible AC or DC charging stations.
- Charging information is displayed in the Digital Cockpit and infotainment system.
- The charging socket has an LED display to indicate charging status.
- Charging may be limited by battery temperature or power availability.
- Interrupting the charging process repeatedly may reduce battery performance over time.
Charging settings: - Configure charging power, limit and departure times via infotainment.
- Set timers for climate control while charging.
- Use reduced charging power for domestic sockets.
- Charging can be adapted to prioritize efficiency or battery preservation.
- Charging profiles can be saved for different locations.
Charging with a home energy management s: - Supports integration with smart home systems.
- Allows dynamic adjustment of charging based on home energy use.
- Requires compatible home charger and configuration.
- Helps optimize energy usage and reduce electricity costs.
Charging cable: - Always use undamaged and approved cables.
- Store cables clean, dry and away from heat or direct sunlight.
- Inspect cable before each use for signs of wear or damage.
- Do not use adapters not approved by the manufacturer.
- Handle plug and cable with dry hands only.
